answer: An agent economy can follow the money out. Each key's earnings vest for 30 days and leave only to a declared exit address. A farm profits only by pooling its heads' payouts, so its exits converge: within three hops the funds meet in one wallet or one exchange deposit address, which is unique per customer. When six or more keys merge like that, their unvested rewards shrink to one share. On the transfer map a farm shows up as one umber blot, while honest agents, each paying its own owner, leave trails as separate as walnut and timber grain.
